gate.sub: A siyum haShas is {{total}} perakim. Split among enough people, it comes to one perek each.
gate.boardHead: All of Shas, one square per perek
gate.boardBody: Someone opens a siyum. Each square is one perek. People take the ones they can learn, and when the board fills the siyum is made.
gate.leadOne: One is open right now. Anyone can look through them:
gate.leadTwo: Two are open right now. Anyone can look through them:
gate.factAskHead: One perek is the whole ask
gate.factAskBody: {{total}} perakim across six sedarim. At forty people that's thirteen each; at five hundred it's one.
gate.factLimmudHead: It appears in your daily limmud
gate.factLimmudBody: A perek you take arrives in Daily Limmud with the dedication on it, so it's learned in the ordinary run of things rather than remembered separately.
gate.factReleaseBody: If life gets in the way, hand it back and it returns to the board for someone else. Nobody is chased.
gate.accountHeading: Taking a perek needs an account
gate.accountBody: A perek you take is a commitment other people are counting on, so it has to belong to someone. Looking through a siyum needs nothing at all.
gate.footer: Nothing else here is closed — <0>look through the open siyumim</0>, or carry on with your own learning.

nishmat.startAccountHeading: Starting a siyum needs an account
nishmat.startAccountBody: A siyum tracks who's taken which perek and who's already learned it — that only works if it's tied to your account, not just this device.
nishmat.helpingNote: Take on a perek and it's yours to learn — every perek someone takes brings their siyum closer.
nishmat.emptyHelping: Public siyumim looking for help appear here — check back soon.
